evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.142: oculōs membrānīs tenuissimīs vestīvit
terms.comment: A description of ours. Membrāna is the thin skin over a part of the body, the skin of an onion or garlic, the slough of a snake (Lewis & Short); plastica follows the lexicon’s māteria plastica (see “plastic”). No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for cling film.

phrases.latin: Catīnum membrānā plasticā obtege et in frīgidārium pōne.
phrases.english: Cover the bowl with cling film and put it in the fridge.

phrases.latin: quae prīmum oculōs membrānīs tenuissimīs vestīvit et saepsit; quās perlūcidās fēcit
phrases.english: which first clothed and fenced the eyes with the thinnest of membranes, and made them transparent
